overview: Fossil-calibrated clocks and Early Cretaceous body fossils are kept separate: modelled crown ages do not become direct fossil first appearances or ecological dominance.

ecology.diet: Primary-producer ecology inferred from angiosperm identity; physiology is not directly preserved
ecology.habitat: Submerged freshwater setting for the sampled Montsechia material
ecology.locomotion: Sessile plant habit inferred; growth was not directly observed
ecology.bodySize: Herbaceous branching shoots in Montsechia; not a clade-wide size bound
ecology.guild: Submerged aquatic primary producer in the sampled Barremian deposits; ancestral ecology unresolved

traits: Leafy flexible axes in the sampled Montsechia material
Closed single-seeded fruits in the sampled Montsechia material
Enclosed ovule-and-fruit evidence used for angiosperm context
evidenceSummary: Clock estimates are calibration-sensitive, while Montsechia supplies specimen-level aquatic morphology; neither alone fixes the crown origin or ancestral ecology.

title.en: Integrated analysis of fossils and molecular divergence time estimates a latest Jurassic origin of angiosperms
title.zh: Integrated analysis of fossils and molecular divergence time estimates a latest Jurassic origin of angiosperms

title.en: A metacalibrated time-tree documents the early rise of flowering plant phylogenetic diversity
title.zh: A metacalibrated time-tree documents the early rise of flowering plant phylogenetic diversity

scope.en: The selected anatomical, relationship or time-estimate material described in this account; no complete species history or distribution is inferred.
scope.zh: 用于本文选取的解剖、关系或时间估计材料，不由此推断完整物种史或分布。

text.zh: 早白垩世的 Montsechia 化石保存了带叶枝轴和封闭的单种子果实。这些身体结构告诉我们当时已有怎样的植物，却没有记录整个类群诞生的瞬间。现生谱系的分子钟则在模型中估计分支时间，两类材料共同构成开花植物起源研究中的不同时间线。
text.en: Early Cretaceous Montsechia fossils preserve leafy axes and closed, single-seeded fruits. Their bodies record plants that existed then, rather than the instant the entire group originated. Molecular clocks estimate branching times from living lineages within models: two different timelines in the study of flowering-plant origins.

title.zh: 保存枝轴与果实的 Montsechia

text.zh: 早白垩世的 Montsechia 材料保存了柔软的带叶枝轴和封闭的单种子果实。这些是具体标本上的结构，可以用于讨论早期被子植物的形态与水生生活。它们没有记录下整个类群诞生的那一刻。
text.en: Early Cretaceous Montsechia material preserves flexible leafy axes and closed single-seeded fruits. These specimen-level structures inform discussion of early angiosperm morphology and aquatic life. They do not record the moment the whole group originated.

text.zh: 分子钟研究把现生谱系的数据与化石校准结合，估计分支发生的时间。这里的“冠群”包括某个类群全部现生成员的最近共同祖先及其后代。不同校准和分析方法会影响估计，所以冠群年代不能直接写成最早化石年代。
text.en: Molecular-clock studies combine data from living lineages with fossil calibrations to estimate branching times. A crown group includes the last common ancestor of all living members and its descendants. Calibration and analysis choices affect the estimate, so a crown age is not a first fossil occurrence.

title.zh: 起源与生态扩张的不同记录
title.en: Different records of origin and ecological expansion

text.zh: 某个年代已经存在开花植物，不等于它们当时已占据各种生态系统。一个水生化石也不能代表所有早期被子植物的祖先生态。把具体标本、模型估计和生态扩张分开，能避免用一个数字讲完一段复杂历史。
text.en: The presence of flowering plants at an age does not establish dominance across ecosystems. One aquatic fossil cannot represent the ancestral ecology of every early angiosperm. Keep specimens, model estimates and ecological expansion separate.

readerLimitations.en: Anatomical observations, interpretations of behaviour and modelled branching times answer different questions. The selected material does not identify a direct ancestor or establish a complete distribution.
readerLimitations.zh: 解剖观察、行为解释与模型中的分支时间回答不同问题。所选材料不指定直接祖先，也不建立完整分布范围。

overview: Cratolirion bognerianum provides an approximately 115 Ma, root-to-flower anatomical sample recovered as a crown monocot without fixing a living-family assignment.

ecology.habitat: Terrestrial Crato setting for the fossil; broad habitats in living monocots
ecology.bodySize: Herbaceous fossil; broad size range across the clade
ecology.guild: Primary producer; no single class-wide ecological guild

traits: Parallel-veined leaf context in many monocots
Crown placement from a morphology matrix
evidenceSummary: Cratolirion directly preserves extensive anatomy and a bounded occurrence; its crown position is analytical and does not establish the monocot origin or one modern family.

geography: Lameta Formation coprolite phytolith assemblage, central India
overview: The profile separates a sampled plastid topology from latest-Cretaceous Lameta phytolith evidence and a regional Neogene phytolith transition; none of these records supplies a single grass origin, universal C4 history or global grassland narrative.

ecology.diet: Photosynthetic primary producer; no family-wide ecological role is inferred from the fossil samples
ecology.habitat: Heterogeneous mixed C3–C4 habitats in the sampled central Great Plains palaeosols; no global habitat is assigned
ecology.bodySize: No family-wide body-size range is inferred from phytolith assemblages
ecology.guild: Primary-producer context only; the evidence does not equate C4 biomass with open-grassland dominance

traits: Diagnostic grass phytolith morphotypes in latest-Cretaceous Lameta coprolites
Chloridoid and other potentially C4 PACMAD short-cell phytoliths in the sampled Great Plains assemblages
Multiple reconstructed C4 origins on the sampled plastid tree
evidenceSummary: Prasad and colleagues supply a contested, locality-bounded phytolith record, Strömberg and McInerney quantify a later regional assemblage shift, and GPWG II supplies a sampled plastid topology. These evidence streams are kept separate from body-fossil first appearances, crown ages and global vegetation cover.

overview: The 65.35 Ma Corral Bluffs fruit and leaflets provide a source-bounded family record, while a taxonomically comprehensive phylogeny revises living subfamily classification. Neither evidence stream fixes crown-Fabaceae age, subfamily placement of the fossil or an origin centre.

ecology.diet: Photosynthetic primary-producer identity inferred from family membership; the Corral Bluffs fruit and leaflets do not directly recover a family-wide ecology
ecology.habitat: Corral Bluffs fossil locality only; no family-wide habitat is assigned
ecology.bodySize: Fruit and leaflet evidence only; no family-wide size range is assigned
ecology.guild: Primary-producer context only; fossil morphology does not establish a family-wide guild

traits: A dated Corral Bluffs fruit and associated leaflets assigned to Fabaceae
Six-subfamily classification supported by a taxonomically broad phylogeny
Fossil family presence kept separate from subfamily assignment and crown-age inference
evidenceSummary: Lyson and colleagues document the dated fossil material, Koenen and colleagues discuss its status as the oldest unequivocal legume fossil, and LPWG supplies the sampled living-family classification. The profile does not infer direct ancestry or continuous global occupancy.
